Let \(q>3\) be a prime power, and for monic squarefree polynomials \(D,D'\in \mathbb F_q[t]\), let \(E_D\) and \(E_{D'}\) be the elliptic curves over \(\mathbb F_q(t)\) given by
\[
E_D: y^2=x^3+x+D(t),\qquad E_{D'}: y^2=x^3+x+D'(t).
\]
Let \(\mathcal X_D\to \mathbb P^1\) and \(\mathcal X_{D'}\to \mathbb P^1\) denote their minimal regular models, and let \(\Sha(E_D)\) and \(\Sha(E_{D'})\) be their Tate--Shafarevich groups. Here \(|\mathcal X_D(\mathbb F_{q^n})|\) denotes the number of \(\mathbb F_{q^n}\)-rational points on \(\mathcal X_D\), and similarly for \(\mathcal X_{D'}\). If \(L(E_D,T)=L(E_{D'},T)\), which of the following is the strongest consequence that follows?

Let \(N\) be a positive integer, and define
\[
H_N=\{(x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^2: x,y>0,\ xy\ge N\}.
\]
Let
\[
I(H_N)=\operatorname{conv}(\mathbb{Z}^2\cap H_N)
\]
be the integer hull of \(H_N\), and let \(f_0(I(H_N))\) denote the number of vertices of \(I(H_N)\). Interpreting Vinogradov notation \(A \ll B\) to mean that \(A\) is bounded above by a constant multiple of \(B\) for all sufficiently large \(N\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the asymptotic behavior of \(f_0(I(H_N))\) as \(N \to \infty\)?

Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and let \(\Lambda_\alpha\) be a Delone set associated with an \(\alpha\)-Kakutani tiling of \(\mathbb{R}\), i.e. a tiling obtained from the interval-splitting rule with subinterval lengths \(\alpha\) and \(1-\alpha\), together with the choice of one point from each tile. Which of the following statements is equivalent to \(\Lambda_\alpha\) being uniformly spread (that is, bounded-displacement equivalent to a lattice in \(\mathbb{R}\))?

Let \(\mathcal H_4\) denote the class of finite, simple, undirected graphs of girth \(8\) (that is, whose shortest cycle has length \(8\)) and with no even hole (induced even cycle) of length at least \(10\). Which of the following is the strongest valid conclusion about graphs in \(\mathcal H_4\)?

Let \(N\in\mathbb N\), let \(T>0\), and consider the initial value problem \(\mathbf y'(t)=\mathbf f(\mathbf y(t))\) for \(t\in[0,T]\) with initial condition \(\mathbf y(0)=\mathbf y_0\), where \(\mathbf f\) is defined on an open set containing \(\mathbb R_+^N\). Here \(\mathbb R_+^N:=\{(x_1,\dots,x_N)\in\mathbb R^N: x_i>0\text{ for all }i\}\) is the positive orthant. Which statement holds for every exact solution with \(\mathbf y_0\in\mathbb R_+^N\)?

For each odd integer \(m\ge 3\) and each integer \(d\ge 2\), let
\[
D_d(m)=\operatorname{Cay}\bigl((\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^d,\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}\bigr),
\]
the Cartesian product of \(d\) consistently oriented \(m\)-cycles. A directed Hamilton cycle is a spanning directed cycle, and a decomposition of the arc set into \(d\) directed Hamilton cycles means a partition of all arcs of \(D_d(m)\) into \(d\) pairwise arc-disjoint directed Hamilton cycles. Which of the following is the strongest existence statement valid in this setting?

A countable discrete group $G$ is called a $W^*$-McDuff group if its group von Neumann algebra $L(G)$ is a McDuff II$_1$ factor. Here, $G$ is called McDuff superrigid in the strongest sense if whenever $L(G)\cong L(H)$ for some group $H$, one has $H\cong G\times A$ for some ICC amenable group $A$ (ICC means every nontrivial conjugacy class is infinite). What is the strongest existence statement that can be proved about countable $W^*$-McDuff groups?

Let \(f\) and \(g\) be H\'enon--Sibony maps of \(\mathbb C^k\), i.e. polynomial automorphisms of \(\mathbb C^k\) of degree \(>1\) whose extensions to \(\mathbb P^k\) have disjoint indeterminacy sets for the map and its inverse. For such a map \(h\), write
\[
K_h^+=\{z\in \mathbb C^k: \{h^n(z)\}_{n\ge 0}\text{ is bounded}\}
\]
for its forward filled set. Assume that \(K_f^+=K_g^+\). Which of the following is the strongest existence statement valid in this setting?

Let $R$ be a ring, let $\mathsf D(R)$ denote the derived category of $R$-modules, and write $\mathsf{pgdim}(-)$ for projective generating dimension. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the inequality between $\mathsf{pgdim}(\mathsf D(R))$ and $\mathsf{pgdim}(R)$ for every ring $R$?

Let \(n,m\ge 1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and \(\beta\ge 0\). Consider the degenerate elliptic operator
\[
L=-\nabla_x\!\cdot\!\bigl(|x|^{2\alpha}\nabla_x\bigr)+|x|^{2\beta}\Delta_y
\qquad \text{on }\mathbb R^n\times \mathbb R^m,
\]
with associated first-order operator \(\nabla_L=(|x|^\alpha\nabla_x,\,|x|^\beta\nabla_y)\). Let \(\mathcal Q\) denote the homogeneous dimension parameter associated with the control geometry of \(L\), and let \(P(\Omega)\) denote the perimeter of a measurable set \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^{n+m}\) with respect to this geometry. Which statement is the strongest one that holds for every measurable set \(\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+m}\) of finite perimeter under these assumptions?

Let \(X\) be an integral projective curve with local complete intersection singularities. Which of the following statements is equivalent to the condition that the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of \(X\) degenerates at the \(E_2\)-page?

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold, and let $K\subset M$ be a Liouville domain, meaning a codimension-$0$ submanifold with smooth boundary for which there exists a vector field $X$ on $K$ such that $\mathcal L_X\omega=\omega$; write $\alpha=\iota_X\omega|_{\partial K}$ for the induced contact form on $\partial K$. Assume that $(M,\omega)$ is symplectically aspherical and that the contact manifold $(\partial K,\alpha)$ is index-bounded. Let $SH_M(K)$ denote the relative symplectic cohomology of $K$ in $M$, and let $\hbar(SH_M(K))$ be its barcode entropy. Let $\varphi_\alpha^t$ denote the Reeb flow on $(\partial K,\alpha)$, and let $h_{\mathrm{top}}(\varphi_\alpha^1)$ be the topological entropy of its time-$1$ map. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative estimate for $\hbar(SH_M(K))$?

Let \(W\) be a Coxeter group, equipped with its Bruhat order, and let \(u,v\in W\) with \(u\le v\). For this pair, let \(d_{u,v}\) and \(g_{u,v}\) denote the two quantities associated to the Bruhat interval \([u,v]=\{x\in W: u\le x\le v\}\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the identity \(d_{u,v}=g_{u,v}\) for every such pair \((u,v)\)?

Let \(g\ge 0\) be an integer, let \(P\subset \mathbb{R}^2\) be a convex lattice polygon (so its vertices lie in \(\mathbb{Z}^2\)), and let \(|\partial P|\) denote the number of lattice points on the boundary of \(P\). Let \(X=\operatorname{Tor}_{\mathbb R}(P)\) be the corresponding real toric surface, with toric boundary divisor, and let \(|\mathcal L_P|\) be the linear system associated with \(P\). Suppose \(\boldsymbol w\subset X\) is a conjugation-invariant set of \(|\partial P|+g-1\) points, where every nonreal point occurs together with its complex conjugate and every such conjugate pair lies on components of the toric boundary divisor of \(X\). Assume also that the reduced tropicalization of \(\boldsymbol w\) (the tropicalized configuration after pairing conjugate points) is in general position. Which of the following is the strongest consequence for the signed count of real curves in \(|\mathcal L_P|\) passing through \(\boldsymbol w\)?

Let \(p\ge 3\), \(\lambda\in(3-3/p,3)\), and \(\sigma>1\). On the three-dimensional torus \(\mathbb T^3=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^3\), consider the cubic wave equation
\[
\partial_{tt}u-\Delta u+u^3=0,\qquad u(x,0)=0,\qquad \partial_tu(x,0)=g(x).
\]
Here \(W^{\alpha,q}(\mathbb T^3)\) denotes the usual \(L^q\)-based Sobolev space, and
\[
S_\lambda=C^\infty(\mathbb T^3)+\{\delta f_\lambda:\ \delta>0\},
\]
where \(f_\lambda\in W^{\sigma-1,p}(\mathbb T^3)\) is defined by its Fourier coefficients
\[
\widehat{f_\lambda}(k)=h(k)\langle k\rangle^{-\sigma+1}|k|^{-\lambda},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z^3,
\]
for a fixed smooth function \(h\) that vanishes near the origin. Which of the following is the strongest conclusion that holds about \(S_\lambda\) and the corresponding solutions?

Let Ω = ℝ^{n+1} \ E, where E ⊂ ℝ^{n+1} is a compact (s, C_0)-Ahlfors regular set, meaning that C_0^{-1} r^s ≤ 𝓗^s(E ∩ B(x,r)) ≤ C_0 r^s for all x ∈ E and 0 < r < diam(E). Let μ := 𝓗^s|_E, and let ω denote the harmonic measure on Ω with pole at infinity. For x ∈ E and 0 < r < diam(E), define
β_2(x,r) := inf_L \left( \frac{1}{μ(B(x,r))} \int_{B(x,r)} \left( \frac{dist(y,L)}{r} \right)^2 \, dμ(y) \right)^{1/2},
where the infimum is over all n-dimensional affine planes L ⊂ ℝ^{n+1}. Assume there exists δ_0 > 0 such that β_2(x,r) ≥ δ_0 for every x ∈ E and every 0 < r < diam(E). What is the strongest statement of the form “there exists c > 0 such that for every such Ω ...”?

Let \(F:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}\) be the integer-valued function under consideration. For a fixed integer \(k\ge 0\), consider the multiset of values \(F(s)\) obtained as \(s\) ranges over the integers satisfying \(2^k\le s<2^{k+1}\). Here \(\operatorname{ord}_2(j)\) denotes the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(j\). Which multiset gives the complete classification of these values, counted with multiplicity?

Let $(M^n,g_0)$, with $3\le n\le 7$, be a smooth manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric $g_0\in L^\infty\cap W^{1,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, smooth on $M\setminus \Omega$ for some compact set $\Omega$, such that $g_0$ is asymptotically flat in $C^2_\delta$ for some $\delta>\frac{n-2}{2}$ and $\operatorname{scal}(g_0)\in L^1(M\setminus \Omega)$. Here an $L^\infty$ metric means a measurable symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor that is uniformly equivalent almost everywhere to some smooth background metric. Assume also that $\operatorname{scal}(g_0)\ge 0$ on $M$ in the distributional sense for $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}\cap L^\infty$ metrics with respect to a smooth background metric. For an $L^\infty$ metric $g$, define its intrinsic distance by
\[
d_g(x,y):=\lim_{p\to+\infty} d_p(x,y),\qquad d_p(x,y)=\left(\inf\left\{\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(M,g)}: u\in \mathrm{Lip}(M),\ u(x)=0,\ u(y)=1\right\}\right)^{-1}.
\]
Which of the following is the strongest conclusion that holds for the ADM mass of $g_0$ and in the equality case?

Let \(A_1,\dots,A_m\) be positive semidefinite \(d\times d\) matrices, and let \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\ge 0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i A_i=I_d\), \(\sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i=1\), and \(\|A_i\|\le M\) for every \(i\in\{1,\dots,m\}\), where \(\|\cdot\|\) denotes the operator norm and \(I_d\) is the \(d\times d\) identity matrix. Which of the following is the strongest statement of the form “there exists ... such that for every ...” that follows from these assumptions?

Let \(e_2=(0,1)\), and consider the two-dimensional inviscid Boussinesq Cauchy problem on \(\mathbb R^2\): \(\partial_t u+u\cdot
abla u+
abla P=	heta e_2\), \(\partial_t	heta+u\cdot
abla	heta=0\), \(
abla\cdot u=0\), \((u,	heta)|_{t=0}=(u_0,	heta_0)\), where \(u=u(t,x)\in\mathbb R^2\), \(	heta=	heta(t,x)\in\mathbb R\), \(P=P(t,x)\in\mathbb R\), \(B^s_{p,r}(\mathbb R^2)\) denotes the standard Besov space, \(B^{\infty}_{p,1}= igcap_{\sigma\in\mathbb R} B^{\sigma}_{p,1}\), \(\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)\) is the Schwartz class, and \(\|(f,g)\|_{B^s_{p,1}}\) denotes the natural product norm. If \(p\in(1,\infty)\) and \(s\in(0,1+2/p)\), which strongest statement holds for every \(\varepsilon>0\)?

Let \(a\le b\le c\), and let \(\Theta_{a,b,c}\) denote the theta graph consisting of two branch vertices joined by three internally disjoint paths of lengths \(a,b,c\). Which of the following statements is equivalent to \(\Theta_{a,b,c}\) being metrizable?

Let \(K_6\) be the complete graph on six vertices. Let \(S(K_6)\) denote the suspension of \(K_6\), i.e. the join of \(K_6\) with two additional vertices not in \(K_6\). Let \(\Lambda^{1,2}(S(K_6))\) denote the set of unordered pairs \(\lambda=\{\gamma,\Sigma\}\) of mutually disjoint subcomplexes of \(S(K_6)\) such that \(\gamma\) is homeomorphic to \(S^1\) and \(\Sigma\) is homeomorphic to \(S^2\). For an embedding \(f\colon S(K_6)\to\mathbb{R}^4\), write \({\rm lk}_2(f(\lambda))\) for the mod-2 linking number of the disjoint images \(f(\gamma)\sqcup f(\Sigma)\) in \(\mathbb{R}^4\). Which of the following is the strongest statement that holds for every such embedding?

Assume that the hypotheses \((f_1'), (f_2), (f_3)\) hold for the energy functional \(J\) considered on \(X=H_0^1(\Omega)\). Here, an unbounded sequence means a sequence that is not bounded in \(X\), and for a critical point \(u\), \(M(J,u)\) denotes the generalized Morse index, i.e. the sum of the dimensions of the negative and null eigenspaces of \(J''(u)\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the critical points of \(J\) under these assumptions?

Let \(P=P_n\) be a set of \(n\) points in \(\mathbb{R}^2\), with no three points collinear, and let the size of the convex hull mean the number of vertices of \(\operatorname{conv}(P)\). Assume that, as \(n\to\infty\), the convex hull size is \(O(n/\log n)\). If a plane graph on \(P\) means a straight-line graph with vertex set \(P\) and no crossing edges, which asymptotic statement gives the strongest valid lower bound on the number of plane graphs on \(P\)?

Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph. Say that $\Gamma$ is $k$-set-homogeneous if, whenever two induced subgraphs of $\Gamma$ on $k$ vertices are isomorphic, some automorphism of $\Gamma$ maps the vertex set of one onto the vertex set of the other. Which statement is equivalent to $\Gamma$ being $k$-set-homogeneous?

Assume \(\ell>n\), \(D\equiv 3\pmod 4\), and \(n\equiv 2\pmod 4\). Let \(E\) be the fixed quadratic imaginary field, let \((\mathbf V,\langle\ ,\ \rangle)\) be a Hermitian space over \(E\) of signature \((2,n)\) at the archimedean place, and let \(\mathbf G=\mathrm U(2,n)\). Let \(\mathbf P=\mathbf M\mathbf N\) be the parabolic subgroup stabilizing a fixed isotropic line, with Levi factor \(\mathbf M\simeq \mathrm{Res}_{E/\mathbb Q}(\mathbf G_m)\times \mathbf U(\mathbf V_0)\), where \(\mathbf V_0\subset \mathbf V\) has signature \((1,n-1)\). Write \(\mathbf Z=[\mathbf N,\mathbf N]\), so that \(\mathbf N(\mathbb Q)/\mathbf Z(\mathbb Q)\) is identified with \(\mathbf V_0\). Let \(E_\ell(g,s)\) be the Eisenstein series under consideration, evaluated at \(s=\ell+1\), and write the adelic variable as \(g=g_f g_\infty\in \mathbf G(\mathbb A_f)\times \mathbf G(\mathbb R)\). Let \(E_{\ell,0}(g)\) denote the \(\mathbf N\)-constant term appearing in its \(\mathbf Z\)-Fourier expansion, let \(\mathcal W_T(g_\infty)\) denote the archimedean \(T\)-th Fourier--Whittaker term, and let \(\nu\) be the similitude character. Which of the following conclusions about the Fourier expansion at \(s=\ell+1\) is valid under these hypotheses?

Let \(\mu\) be a signed Radon measure on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Say that \(\mu\) has a unique blow-up at \(x\) if there exists a Radon measure \(\mu_x\) such that, for every sequence \(r_j\to 0^+\), after passing to a subsequence one has
\[
\mu_{x,r_j}:=\frac{1}{|\mu|(B_{r_j}(x))}(\tau_{x,r_j})_\#\mu \overset{*}{\rightharpoonup} c\,\mu_x
\]
for some constant \(c\neq 0\), where \(\tau_{x,r}(y)=(y-x)/r\) and \(|\mu|\) is the total variation measure of \(\mu\). For points \(x\) with a unique blow-up, let \(D_x\subset \mathbb{R}^n\) denote the distinguished linear subspace associated with that blow-up, and for \(k\in\{0,1,\dots,n\}\) define the \(k\)-stratum by
\[
\mathcal S_\mu^k:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\text{\(\mu\) has a unique blow-up at \(x\) and }\dim D_x=k\}.
\]
A \(k\)-dimensional Lipschitz graph means the graph of a Lipschitz map from a \(k\)-dimensional affine subspace into its orthogonal complement. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the structure of \(\mathcal S_\mu^k\) and its tangent planes under the assumptions above?

Let $G_2$ be the compact exceptional Lie group, and let $BG_2$ denote its classifying space. For integers $k$ and $k'$, let $\mathcal{G}_k$ denote the gauge group (the topological group of bundle automorphisms over $S^4$) of the principal $G_2$-bundle over $S^4$ classified by $k\in \pi_4(BG_2)\cong \mathbb{Z}$. Writing $(a,b)$ for the greatest common divisor and $\simeq_{(p)}$ for $p$-local homotopy equivalence, what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_k$ and $\mathcal{G}_{k'}$?

Let \(C_n\) be the cycle graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(W(C_n)\) denote its whiskered graph, obtained by attaching to each vertex of \(C_n\) a new leaf adjacent only to that vertex. Let \(G=W(C_n)\), and let \(I(G)\subseteq \mathbb{K}[V(G)]\) be its edge ideal, i.e. the ideal generated by \(uv\) for edges \(\{u,v\}\in E(G)\). For \(q\ge 1\), let \(I(G)^{[q]}\) denote the \(q\)-th squarefree power of \(I(G)\), meaning the ideal generated by squarefree products of \(q\) pairwise disjoint edge monomials. Let \(\operatorname{reg}\) denote Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity. Which exact formula holds for every integer \(q\) with \(1\le q\le n\)?

Let \((X,d,\nu)\) be the metric-measure-space model of a noncollapsed \(\mathbb F\)-limit metric soliton, and let \((\mathcal R_X,\mathfrak g,f_0)\) denote its regular part, i.e. the smooth locus where the Riemannian metric \(\mathfrak g\) is defined (so its Ricci tensor and scalar curvature \(R\) are defined there). Assume that the Ricci curvature of \(\mathfrak g\) is nonnegative at every point of \(\mathcal R_X\) and is not identically zero on \(\mathcal R_X\). Which of the following is the strongest valid quantitative estimate for the scalar curvature on \(\mathcal R_X\)?

Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectrum, and let $\mathrm{T}\Sigma(R)$ denote its topological symmetric homology (i.e. the construction associated to the symmetric crossed simplicial group $\Delta\Sigma$). Which $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-ring-spectrum construction on $R$ is $\mathrm{T}\Sigma(R)$ canonically characterized as?

For each \(r\in\{0,1,2\}\) and \(k\ge 3\) (with \(k\ge 4\) when \(r=2\)), let \(U_{k,r}=U_{k,k+r}\) be the unicyclic graph obtained from the tree \(T_{3,k,k+r}\) by adding the edge \(v_1a_{2,1}\), where \(v_1\) is the distinguished exceptional branch vertex, and \(v_2a_{2,1}b_{2,1}\) is one chosen pendant path of length \(2\) (a \(P_2\)-arm) among the \(k\) such arms attached at \(v_2\) (the \(k\)-bundle at \(v_2\)). If \(I(U_{k,r};x)=\sum_{i=0}^{\alpha} s_i x^i\) is its independence polynomial, where \(\alpha=\alpha(U_{k,r})\) is the independence number, and where a sequence is log-concave if \(s_i^2\ge s_{i-1}s_{i+1}\), which strongest statement holds about the coefficient sequence \((s_i)\), in particular about the penultimate log-concavity inequality \(s_{\alpha-1}^2\ge s_{\alpha-2}s_{\alpha}\)?

Let
\[
\mathcal H[1]=\begin{pmatrix}
 x_1&x_2&\cdots &x_n&x_{n+1}\\
 x_2&x_3&\cdots &x_{n+1}&x_{n+2}\\
 \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\
 x_n&x_{n+1}&\cdots &x_{2n-1}&x_{2n}\\
 x_{n+1}&x_{n+2}&\cdots &x_{2n}&0
\end{pmatrix}
\]
be the \((n+1)\times(n+1)\) Hankel-type matrix with bottom-right entry equal to \(0\), and let \(I=I_n(\mathcal H[1])\) be the ideal generated by its \(n\times n\) minors. Which description gives the complete minimal generating set of the defining ideal of the special fiber ring \(\mathcal F(I)\)?

Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $G$ be an algebraic group over $k$, and let $\mathcal H(k)$ denote the pointed unstable $\#A^1$-homotopy category of simplicial Nisnevich sheaves on smooth $k$-schemes. Write $\pi_0^{\#A^1}(G)$ for the Nisnevich sheaf of $\#A^1$-connected components of $G$. If $\mathcal P \to \mathcal X$ is any Nisnevich locally trivial $G$-torsor in $\mathcal H(k)$, and $BG$ is the classifying space of $G$, what is the strongest statement that can be proved about every such $G$ and every such torsor?

Let $p\ge 1$, let $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ denote the Schwartz class on $\mathbb R^2$, and let $\|\cdot\|_p$ denote the usual $L^p(\mathbb R^2)$ norm. For $t>0$, define the circular averaging operators
\[
A_t f(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(x_1-t\cos\alpha,\,x_2-t\sin\alpha)\,d\alpha,
\]
and let $V_2^I A f$ denote the $2$-variation in the parameter $t$ over a fixed interval $I$ of the family $\{A_t f\}_{t\in I}$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about $V_2^I A f$ acting on $f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$?

Let \(X\) be a connected Nagata \(J\)-2 scheme. For each irreducible component of \(X\), let \(\tilde X_i\) denote its normalization, and let \(Z\) be the singular locus of the reduced scheme \(X_{\mathrm{red}}\) (where \(X_{\mathrm{red}}\) is the underlying reduced scheme of \(X\)). Write \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{p\acute{e}t}}\) for the pro-\'etale fundamental group and \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}\) for the \(\'etale\) fundamental group; a Noohi coproduct or Noohi quotient is taken in the category of Noohi topological groups. Which of the following is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of a construction of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{p\acute{e}t}}(X)\) from these groups?

Let $B_\rho$ denote the ball of radius $\rho$ centered at the origin, and for $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$ let $B_r(x_0)$ be the ball of radius $r$ centered at $x_0$. Let $\partial B_1$ be the unit sphere, $\chi_{\{w>0\}}$ the indicator of the positivity set of $w$, and $\partial\{w>0\}$ the boundary of that positivity set. For a function $v$, define the Alt--Caffarelli--Friedman functional
\[
\Phi(v,x_0,r)=\frac{1}{r^4}\left(\int_{B_r(x_0)}\frac{|\nabla v_+|^2}{|x-x_0|^{n-2}}\right)\left(\int_{B_r(x_0)}\frac{|\nabla v_-|^2}{|x-x_0|^{n-2}}\right),
\]
where $v_+=\max\{v,0\}$ and $v_-=\max\{-v,0\}$. For $e\in\partial B_1$ and $h\in(0,1)$, define the finite difference quotient
\[
w_{e,h}(x)=\frac{w(x+he)-w(x)}{h}.
\]
Suppose $w\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$ is nonnegative, satisfies $\Delta w=f$ for some $f\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$, and $\operatorname{supp}(f-\chi_{\{w>0\}})\subset B_4$. What is the strongest statement asserting the existence of a constant, uniform in the free-boundary point $x_0$ and the scales $1<r<R$, for the quantity $\Phi(w_{e,h},x_0,\cdot)$ when $e\in\partial B_1$ is arbitrary?

Let \(F\subset S^3\) be a closed surface, and let \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) be the two components of \(S^3\setminus F\). Define the Heegaard deficiency of \(F\) by
\[
\delta(F)=g(M_1)+g(M_2)-g(F),
\]
where \(g(M_i)\) denotes the Heegaard genus of \(M_i\) and \(g(F)\) denotes the genus of \(F\). For a knot \(K\subset S^3\), let \(c(K;F)\) denote the surface crossing number of \(K\) with respect to \(F\), i.e. the minimal number of crossings among all regular diagrams of \(K\) obtained by isotoping \(K\) into a regular neighborhood of \(F\). If \(t(K)\) is the tunnel number of \(K\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the quantitative lower bound for \(c(K;F)\)?

Let \(C\) be a complex projective integral curve with planar singularities, let \(g\) be its geometric genus, let \(B\) be a versal deformation space of \(C\), and let \(B^{\delta}\subset B\) be the \(\delta\)-constant stratum, i.e. the reduced closed subscheme parametrising curves with the same \(\delta\)-invariant as \(C\). Let \(M_g(C,[C])\) be the 0-dimensional moduli space of genus \(g\) stable maps representing \([C]\). If \(m([C],B^{\delta})\) denotes the multiplicity of the point \([C]\) in \(B^{\delta}\), and \(\operatorname{len}(M_g(C,[C]))\) denotes the length of the local scheme \(M_g(C,[C])\), which of the following statements is equivalent to the equality
\[
m([C],B^{\delta})=\operatorname{len}(M_g(C,[C]))?
\]

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and for integers $n,D\ge 1$ let $\Hilb_D(\mathbb A_k^n)$ denote the Hilbert scheme of zero-dimensional subschemes of $\mathbb A_k^n$ of degree $D$. Which of the following is the strongest statement that holds about irreducible components of these Hilbert schemes?

For each positive integer \(n\), let \(\mathbb{M}_n\) denote the \(n\)-th finite approximation of the standard slit carpet: start with the unit square \([0,1]^2\), and for every dyadic subsquare of side length \(2^{-k}\) with \(k\le n\), remove the central vertical slit of length half the side length; equip the remaining set with its shortest-path metric. Let \(C_n\) denote the optimal Euclidean distortion, i.e. the least bi-Lipschitz distortion of an embedding of \(\mathbb{M}_n\) into some Euclidean space \(\mathbb{R}^N\). As \(n \to \infty\), which asymptotic statement about \(C_n\) holds?

Let \(f(x,y)=x+y+(x-y)^2\). For a finite set \(A\subset\mathbb{R}\), write
\[
A+A=\{a+a':a,a'\in A\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
f(A,A)=\{f(a,a'):a,a'\in A\}.
\]
What is the strongest existence statement that can be asserted about finite subsets of \(\mathbb{R}\) for this polynomial map?

Let \(\mathcal S\) be a dissociated set of positive integers, meaning that all finite subset sums of distinct elements of \(\mathcal S\) are different (equivalently, if \(\sum_{s\in F}\varepsilon_s s=0\) for some finite \(F\subseteq \mathcal S\) with coefficients \(\varepsilon_s\in\{-1,0,1\}\), then all \(\varepsilon_s=0\)). For \(n\ge 1\), define \(\mathcal S(n)=\mathcal S\cap\{1,2,\dots,n\}\), and let \(\log_2\) denote the base-2 logarithm. As \(n\to\infty\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the asymptotic upper bound for \(|\mathcal S(n)|\)?

Let \(X\subset \mathbb{R}^n\) be a connected unbounded domain with \(C^2\) boundary, and let \(\nu\) denote the outward unit normal along \(\partial X\). Write \(H\) for the mean curvature of \(\partial X\) with respect to \(\nu\), and assume that \(X\) is mean convex on \(\partial X\), i.e. \(H\ge 0\) everywhere on \(\partial X\). If the boundary \(\partial X\) is disconnected, which of the following is the strongest conclusion that must hold?

Fix an integer \(d\ge 2\). A graph is called \(K_{2d+1}\)-free if it contains no complete subgraph on \(2d+1\) vertices. For a graph \(\Gamma\) with \(n\) vertices, let \(P_\Gamma(x)\) denote the monic polynomial characterized by
\[
(-u)^n P_\Gamma\!\left(-1-\frac1u\right)=\sum_{k\ge 0} c_k u^k,
\]
where \(c_k\) is the number of \(k\)-vertex cliques of \(\Gamma\). A Salem polynomial is a monic integer polynomial whose roots consist of exactly two real reciprocal roots off the unit circle and all remaining roots on the unit circle. Which statement gives the strongest existence conclusion valid for every integer \(d\ge 2\)?

Let \(1<p\le 3\), and work in two spatial dimensions \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\). Suppose \(Q=Q(x,y)\) is a fixed profile, \(\mathcal L\) is a fixed linear operator, and \(\langle f,g\rangle\) denotes the \(L^2(\mathbb R^2)\) inner product. Write \((Q^p)_x=\partial_x(Q^p)\), and \(\nabla Q=(Q_x,Q_y)\), so the condition \(\langle v,\nabla Q\rangle=0\) means \(\langle v,Q_x\rangle=\langle v,Q_y\rangle=0\). When \(p=3\), \(\Lambda Q\) denotes the scaling derivative of \(Q\). Assume that \(v=v(t,x,y)\) solves
\[
\partial_t v=\mathcal L\partial_x v-(p-1)\frac{\langle v,(Q^p)_x\rangle}{\|Q\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}^2}Q,
\]
and that for every \(t\),
\[
\langle v,Q\rangle=0,\qquad \langle v,\nabla Q\rangle=0,
\]
with the additional condition in the endpoint case \(p=3\) that
\[
\langle v,\Lambda Q\rangle=0.
\]
Which of the following is the strongest consequence that follows for the virial-type quantity \(\int_{\mathbb R^2} x\,v(t,x,y)^2\,dx\,dy\)?

Let \(\Omega,\tilde\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^n\) be uniformly convex bounded domains with smooth boundaries, with \(\tilde\Omega\Subset B_1(0)\), where \(B_1(0)=\{p\in\mathbb{R}^n:|p|<1\}\). Let \(f=f(x,p)\) belong to the class
\[
\mathscr A:=\{g\in C^{2+\alpha}(\overline\Omega\times\overline{\tilde\Omega}) : g\text{ is concave in }x\}.
\]
Assume that the oscillation of \(f\), as well as \(|D_x f|\) and \(|D_{xp}f|\), are sufficiently small on \(\overline\Omega\times\overline{\tilde\Omega}\). What is the strongest existence statement that follows for the prescribed mean-curvature type equation
\[
\operatorname{div}\!\left(\frac{Du}{\sqrt{1-|Du|^2}}\right)=f(x,Du)+c\quad \text{in }\Omega,
\]
with second boundary condition \(Du(\Omega)=\tilde\Omega\)?

Let \(\{0=\ell_1<\ell_2<\dots<\ell_n\}\) be an LM ruler with \(n\) marks, where the marks are integers listed in increasing order. Which of the following is the strongest universal lower bound on its largest mark \(\ell_n\)?

Let $(F_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the Fibonacci numbers, defined by $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$, and $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n$. Every integer $N\ge 1$ has a unique Zeckendorf representation
\[
N=\sum_{i=2}^k \varepsilon_i F_i,
\]
where $\varepsilon_i\in\{0,1\}$, $\varepsilon_k=1$, and $\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_{i+1}=0$. Write $\operatorname{rev}(Z(N))=\varepsilon_2\varepsilon_3\cdots \varepsilon_k$ for the Zeckendorf digits read from least significant to most significant, and let $\widetilde Z(N)=\operatorname{rev}(Z(N))\,\#^{\omega}$, where $\#\notin\{0,1\}$ is a padding symbol.

Let $u\ge 1$ and $q\ge 2$ be integers, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of non-empty binary words, let $L=\max\{|f|:f\in\mathcal F\}$, and fix $M\ge L$. Define
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathcal F}^{(M)}=\{N\ge 1:\text{ the prefix of length }M\text{ of }\widetilde Z(N)\text{ contains no factor from }\mathcal F\},
\]
and
\[
S_u^{(M)}=\{n\ge 0: u q^n\in \mathcal K_{\mathcal F}^{(M)}\}.
\]
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about $S_u^{(M)}$?

What is the strongest statement that holds for every smooth projective complex variety \(X\) defined over \(\mathbb{R}\), with nonempty real locus \(X(\mathbb{R})\neq\varnothing\) (where \(X(\mathbb{R})\) denotes the set of real points of \(X\))? Here, saying that the universal cover \(\tilde X\) is \emph{real holomorphically convex} means that, for a lift \(\tilde\sigma\) of the real structure to \(\tilde X\), there exists a Stein space \(\tilde Y\) with an antiholomorphic involution \(\tilde\sigma_Y\) and a proper equivariant holomorphic map \((\tilde X,\tilde\sigma)\to(\tilde Y,\tilde\sigma_Y)\).

Let \(k\ge 6\) be an integer and let \(G\) be a graph with minimum degree at least \(k\). Here, a cycle of length \(r \pmod k\) means a cycle whose length is congruent to \(r\) modulo \(k\); \(K_{k+1}\) is the complete graph on \(k+1\) vertices; \(K_{k,k}\) is the complete bipartite graph with both parts of size \(k\); an end-block of \(G\) is a block containing at most one cut-vertex of \(G\), and a non-end-block is any block of \(G\) that is not an end-block; and \(\mathcal H_k\) denotes the exceptional graph family \(\mathcal H_k\). Which description exactly classifies the graphs \(G\) that do not contain a cycle of length \(r \pmod k\) for every even integer \(r\)?

Let \(G\) be a finitely generated LERF (subgroup separable) group, and suppose that \(G\) is the fundamental group of a graph of groups whose vertex groups are virtually free and whose edge groups are virtually cyclic. Write \(\widehat{G}\) for the profinite completion of \(G\). If \(\widehat{G}\) splits as a non-trivial free profinite product, what is the strongest conclusion that follows about \(G\)?

Let $X$ be a smooth proper variety over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic $0$, and let $\mathcal A\subset \mathrm D^b_{\mathrm{coh}}(X)$ (the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X$) be an admissible subcategory. Let $Z\subset X$ be the set-theoretic support of $\mathcal A$, i.e. the union of the supports of all objects of $\mathcal A$, and assume $Z\ne X$. Which of the following is the strongest conclusion that holds for morphisms from $Z$ to abelian varieties, and for irreducible components of $Z$ meeting the other components only in dimension $0$?

Let \(\Sigma\subset \mathbb{S}^3\subset \mathbb{R}^4\) be a smooth embedded surface in the round 3-sphere, with genus at least \(1\). For \(v\in \mathring{B}^4=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^4:|v|<1\}\), let
\[
F_v(x)=(1-|v|^2)\frac{x-v}{|x-v|^2}-v
\]
be the associated conformal transformation of \(\mathbb{S}^3\), and set \(\Sigma_v:=F_v(\Sigma)\). If \(\mathbb{S}^3\setminus \Sigma=A\cup A^*\) is the decomposition into connected components, let \(A_v:=F_v(A)\), let \(d_v\) be the signed distance to \(\Sigma_v\) (positive on \(A_v\), negative on the other component), and define
\[
\Sigma_{(v,t)}=\partial\{x\mid d_v(x)<t\}, \qquad (v,t)\in\mathring{B}^4\times[-\pi,\pi].
\]
Thus \(\{\Sigma_{(v,t)}\}_{(v,t)\in \mathring{B}^4\times[-\pi,\pi]}\) is the canonical five-parameter family of \(\Sigma\). Which quantitative area estimate holds for this family, and in which case does equality occur?

Let ${\mathbb R}^d\curvearrowright \Omega$ be a free action on a compact metrizable space $\Omega$, where $\varphi^p(x)$ denotes the action of $p\in\mathbb R^d$ on $x\in\Omega$. Let $X$ be a flat Cantor transversal, and define the transversal groupoid by
\[
R_\varphi=\{(\varphi^p(x),x): x,\varphi^p(x)\in X\text{ and }p\in \mathbb R^d\}.
\]
Assume that $R_\varphi$ is minimal and principal. Which strongest conclusion holds for $R_\varphi$ and for every twist $\Sigma$ on $R_\varphi$?

Let \(Y\) be a closed 3-manifold obtained by Dehn surgery on a \((1,1)\) knot in \(S^3\) (that is, a knot admitting a 1-bridge presentation with respect to a genus-1 Heegaard splitting of \(S^3\)). In the usual formulation of the L-space conjecture, let \((a)\) mean that \(Y\) is not an L-space, \((b)\) mean that \(\pi_1(Y)\) is left-orderable, and \((c)\) mean that \(Y\) admits a coorientable taut foliation. Which relation among \((a)\), \((b)\), and \((c)\) holds for such \(Y\)?

Let $b>0$, and let $g=g(t,r)$, $\tilde g=\tilde g(t,r)$, $u=u(t,r)$, $\tilde u=\tilde u(t,r)$, and $\nu=\nu(t,r)$ be functions defined for $0<r\le b$ (with $t$ arbitrary) such that, with subscripts denoting partial derivatives, they satisfy
\[
\nu_t-\Big(\tfrac12\,\tilde g\,u\Big)_r=-\tfrac12\,\tilde g_r\,\tilde u,
\qquad
 g_r=\frac1r\,g\,(u-\tilde u)^2,
\qquad
\tilde g_r=\frac1r\,(g-\tilde g),
\]
and the normalization at the outer radius $r=b$ is $g(t,b)=1$. For every fixed $t$, which statement is guaranteed to hold for all $r\in(0,b]$?

Fix the following notation: for each real number \(C>1\), let \(p_C\in(0,1/2)\) be a specified parameter depending on \(C\); let \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{HMS}}\) be a fixed constant; and for positive integers \(\ell,m\), let \(R(\ell,m)\) denote the Ramsey number, i.e. the least integer \(n\) such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph \(K_n\) contains either a red copy of \(K_\ell\) or a blue copy of \(K_m\). Which of the following is the strongest valid lower-bound statement for \(R(\ell,C\ell)\) as \(\ell\to\infty\)?

For the 2D gravity-capillary water-wave problem for an incompressible fluid in a moving domain \(\mathcal D_t\) lying between the fixed bottom \(\Gamma_b=\mathbb R\times\{x_2=0\}\) and an upper free surface \(\Gamma_t\), with \(e_2=(0,1)\), governed in \(\mathcal D_t\) by
\[
\partial_t u+u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla p+ge_2=0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,
\]
and with the free surface moving with the fluid velocity and satisfying the capillary pressure condition \(p=\sigma H\) on \(\Gamma_t\), as well as the impermeable bottom boundary condition \(u\cdot e_2=0\) on \(\Gamma_b\), initial fluid domain \(\mathcal D_0=\mathbb R\times(0,2)\), and vorticity \(\omega(t,x)=\partial_1u_2-\partial_2u_1\), what is the strongest statement of the form “there exists \(\cdots\) such that for all \(\cdots\)” about the growth of \(\|\nabla\omega(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal D_t)}\) for solutions whose initial velocity is \(u_0=\varepsilon v_0\)?

Let $n\ge 3$, and let $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be a convex viscosity solution of
$$\det(D^2u)=f\quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n,$$
where $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies the following assumption $(H)$: there exist a positive periodic function $f_p$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, constants $d_0,d_1>0$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\beta>2$, and $a_1,\dots,a_n>0$ such that
$$d_0^{-1}\le f_p\le d_0,\qquad [f_p]_{C^\alpha(\mathbb{R}^n)}\le d_0,\qquad f_p(x+a_i e_i)=f_p(x)
\ \text{ for all }x\in\mathbb{R}^n,$$
for $i=1,\dots,n$, and for some bounded open set $\mathcal O\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$f\in C(\mathbb{R}^n)\cap C^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\overline{\mathcal O}),$$
and, for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$,
$$|x|^{\beta}|(f-f_p)(x)|+|x|^{\beta+\alpha}[f-f_p]_{C^{\alpha}(\overline{B_{|x|/2}(x)})}\le d_1.$$ 
Also, let $\mathcal A$ denote the set of real symmetric positive definite $n\times n$ matrices $A$ such that
$$\det(A)=\frac{1}{a_1\cdots a_n}\int_{\prod_{i=1}^n[0,a_i]} f(x)\,dx.$$ 
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the uniform asymptotic behavior of $u$?

Let \(G\) be a countably infinite discrete abelian group acting freely on the circle \(\mathbb T\) (that is, if \(g\cdot x=x\) for some \(x\in \mathbb T\), then \(g=e\)). Let \(A=C(\mathbb T)\rtimes G\) be the crossed-product \(C^*\)-algebra associated to this action. Here “minimal” means that every \(G\)-orbit in \(\mathbb T\) is dense. Which of the following is the strongest consequence of these assumptions, including the additional structure in the non-minimal case?

Let $Z$ be an arbitrary finite abelian group of order $N$. For $k$, let $\chi(Z,k)$ denote the chromatic number of the undirected random Cayley graph on vertex set $Z$ obtained by choosing $k$ elements of $Z$ independently and uniformly with replacement, and joining distinct vertices $x,y\in Z$ whenever $x-y$ lies in the sampled set or in its negation (loops ignored, multiplicities suppressed). What is the strongest asymptotic statement, as $N\to\infty$, about the random quantity $\chi\bigl(Z,\tfrac{1}{64}\log N\bigr)$?

Let $\pi\colon \mathcal{X}\to \mathbb{D}$ be a projective morphism to the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, with central fiber $\mathcal{X}_0=\pi^{-1}(0)$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a divisor such that $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{X}_0+\mathcal{B})$ is a log Calabi--Yau pair over $\mathbb{D}$ (so $K_{\mathcal{X}}+\mathcal{X}_0+\mathcal{B}$ is trivial over $\mathbb{D}$), and assume that $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{X}_0)$ is plt (purely log terminal). For each $t\in \mathbb{D}^*=\mathbb{D}\setminus\{0\}$, write $\mathcal{X}_t=\pi^{-1}(t)$ and $\mathcal{B}_t=\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{X}_t}$. Suppose that for every $t\in \mathbb{D}^*$, the fiber pair $(\mathcal{X}_t,\mathcal{B}_t)$ is toric, meaning that $\mathcal{X}_t$ is a projective toric variety and $\mathcal{B}_t$ is its reduced torus-invariant boundary. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the special fiber pair $(\mathcal{X}_0,\mathcal{B}_0)$?

Let $G$ be a directed acyclic graph with netflow vector $\mathbf a$, and let $\mathcal F_G(\mathbf a)$ denote the flow polytope of nonnegative flows on $G$ with netflow vector $\mathbf a$. Suppose $(\hat G,\hat{\mathbf a},\hat{\mathfrak F})$ is any framed augmentation of $(G,\mathbf a)$, where an augmentation is obtained by adding inflow/outflow vertices and edges so that $\hat{\mathbf a}$ is $1$ on inflow vertices, negative on outflow vertices, and $0$ on the original vertices of $G$, with contracting all added inflow/outflow edges recovering $(G,\mathbf a)$; and a framing is a choice of total orders on the incoming and outgoing edges at each internal vertex, together with a total order on the inflow vertices. From this data, let $\mathrm{Layerings}(\hat G,\hat{\mathbf a},\hat{\mathfrak F})$ denote the associated set of layerings (compatible collections of source-to-sink routes with the prescribed starts and ends), and for each such $\mathcal L$ let $\check D_1(\mathcal L)$ be its associated simplex. Define the framing triangulation by
\[
\mathcal T(\hat G,\hat{\mathbf a},\hat{\mathfrak F}) := \{\check D_1(\mathcal L): \mathcal L\in \mathrm{Layerings}(\hat G,\hat{\mathbf a},\hat{\mathfrak F})\}.
\]
What is the strongest statement that holds for every such $G$, $\mathbf a$, and framed augmentation $(\hat G,\hat{\mathbf a},\hat{\mathfrak F})$?

Let $F$ be a finite triple system, i.e. a finite $3$-uniform hypergraph. After deleting all isolated vertices of $F$, suppose that the resulting hypergraph is linear (any two hyperedges meet in at most one vertex), every hyperedge-vertex in its Levi graph (the bipartite incidence graph of vertices and hyperedges) is incident with a bridge, and every Berge cycle of $F$ has even length, where a Berge cycle is an alternating cyclic sequence $v_1,e_1,v_2,e_2,\dots,v_k,e_k,v_1$ of distinct vertices $v_i$ and distinct hyperedges $e_i$ such that $\{v_i,v_{i+1}\}\subseteq e_i$ for each $i$ (indices mod $k$). Which statement is equivalent to these conditions? Here the chromatic number of a triple system is the least number of vertex-colors with no monochromatic hyperedge.

Let \(g\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) with \(g(0)=0\). For \(s>0\), define
\[
X^s(\mathbb R^2):=\{f\in H^s(\mathbb R^2):\partial_x^{-1}f\in H^s(\mathbb R^2),\ \partial_x f\in H^s(\mathbb R^2)\},
\]
where \(\partial_x^{-1}f\) is the Fourier multiplier with symbol \((i\xi)^{-1}\). Let \(s\ge 2\), let \(u_0\in X^s(\mathbb R^2)\), and let
\[
 u\in C([0,T_{u_0}^*);X^s(\mathbb R^2))\cap C^1([0,T_{u_0}^*);X^{s-2}(\mathbb R^2))
\]
be the unique solution on its maximal existence interval \([0,T_{u_0}^*)\) of
\[
\begin{cases}
u_t+\gamma u u_x+G*\partial_x\left(\frac12 g(u)+\frac\gamma2 u_x^2-\frac\gamma2 u^2\right)+G*v_y=0,\quad (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2,\\
\nu_y=v_x,\\
u\big|_{t=0}=u_0(x,y),\quad (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2.
\end{cases}
\]
Assume that the maximal existence time is finite, \(T_{u_0}^*<\infty\). Writing \(\nabla u=(u_x,u_y)\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the blow-up behavior of \(u\) as \(t\to T_{u_0}^{*-}\)?

Let $(Y,\xi)$ be a contact integer homology sphere that is an $L$-space and has nonzero Heegaard Floer contact invariant, where an integer homology sphere means a closed oriented $3$-manifold with the same integral homology as $S^3$. Consider the contact cosmetic surgery conjecture for nontrivial Legendrian knots in $(Y,\xi)$, where “nontrivial” means that the underlying smooth knot type is not the unknot, and the conjecture asserts that such a knot admits no cosmetic contact surgeries. Which of the following is the strongest conclusion that holds under these hypotheses? Here, for the smooth knot type $K$ underlying a Legendrian knot $L$, $\tau_Y(K)$ denotes the Heegaard Floer $\tau$-invariant in $Y$, $g(K)$ the Seifert genus, and $\overline{tb}(K)$ the maximal Thurston–Bennequin invariant among Legendrian representatives of $K$.

Let $X=V(f)\subset \mathbb P^n$ be a smooth cubic hypersurface with $n\ge 3$, and assume that $\dim(\mathcal D_2(f))=1$, where $\mathcal D_k(f):=\{P\in \mathbb P^n:\operatorname{rank} H_f(P)\le k\}$ for the Hessian matrix $H_f$ of $f$. Here, $f$ is said to be of Thom--Sebastiani type if, after a change of coordinates, it can be written as $f=f_1(x_0,\dots,x_k)+f_2(x_{k+1},\dots,x_n)$ for some $0\le k\le n-1$. Which description gives the complete classification of the possible forms of $f$ under this hypothesis?

Fix q\ge 2. Let
\[\mathcal D_q=\{(k_1,k_2,\ldots)\in \mathcal T: k_i\le q\text{ for all }i\},\]
where
\[\mathcal T=\{(k_1,k_2,\ldots): k_1\ge 2,\ k_i\in\mathbb N\ (i\ge 2),\text{ and if }k_1=2\text{ then }k_s\ge 2\text{ for some }s\ge 2\}.\]
Also let \(\eta((k_1,k_2,\ldots)):=\zeta^\star(k_1,k_2,\ldots)\), the corresponding infinite multiple zeta-star value. If, for a subset \(S\subseteq \mathbb R\), one writes \(S/S:=\{x/y:x,y\in S\}\), which of the following gives the complete classification of the quotient set \(\eta(\mathcal D_q)/\eta(\mathcal D_q)\)?

Work in the usual ZFC framework. Let \(G\) be a non-locally finite group, i.e. a group having some finitely generated infinite subgroup. For any set \(A\), write \(A^G\) for the set of functions \(G\to A\), equipped with the prodiscrete topology (the product topology when each copy of \(A\) is discrete). A map \(\tau:A^G\to A^G\) is a finite-memory cellular automaton if there exist a finite set \(M\subset G\) and a local rule \(\mu:A^M\to A\) such that for every configuration \(x\in A^G\) and every \(g\in G\), the value \(\tau(x)(g)\) depends only on the restriction of \(x\) to \(gM\). If \(K\) is a field and \(V\) is a \(K\)-vector space, a finite-memory linear cellular automaton \(\tau:V^G\to V^G\) is such a cellular automaton that is also \(K\)-linear. Which statement gives the strongest existence conclusion valid under these assumptions?

Let \(\Gamma\) be a Moore graph of diameter \(2\) and degree \(57\), and let \(\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)\) denote its automorphism group. Which strongest conclusion holds about \(\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)\)?

Assume the standing hypotheses \((H_1)\) and \((H_2)\) hold, let \(\mu_1,\mu_2>0\), and set
\[
\mathcal M:=(-\sqrt{\mu_1\mu_2},\min\{\mu_1,\mu_2\})\cup(\max\{\mu_1,\mu_2\},+\infty).
\]
For each \(l=1,\dots,k\), assume \(P(\xi_l)=Q(\xi_l)=0\) and, in a neighborhood of \(\xi_l\),
\[
P(x)=\sum_{i=1}^N p_{li}(x_i-\xi_{l,i})^2+O(|x-\xi_l|^3),\qquad Q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^N q_{li}(x_i-\xi_{l,i})^2+O(|x-\xi_l|^3).
\]
Also set
\[
\sigma_1:=\sqrt{\frac{\beta-\mu_2}{\beta^2-\mu_1\mu_2}},\qquad \sigma_2:=\sqrt{\frac{\beta-\mu_1}{\beta^2-\mu_1\mu_2}}.
\]
Let \(H:=H^1(\mathbb R^N)\times H^1(\mathbb R^N)\), and let \(E_\lambda\subset H\) be the corresponding correction space, namely the orthogonal complement of the span of the translation modes associated with the rescaled profiles. Consider for \(N\in\{2,3\}\) the \(L^2\)-normalized system
\[
\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
-\triangle \bar u+(P(x)+\lambda)\bar u=\mu_1\bar u^3+\beta\bar u\bar v^2, & \text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\
-\triangle \bar v+(Q(x)+\lambda)\bar v=\mu_2\bar v^3+\beta\bar v\bar u^2, & \text{in }\mathbb R^N,
\end{array}\right.
\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^N}(\bar u^2+\bar v^2)=\rho^2,
\]
with fixed data \(k\), \(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_k\), \(p_{li},q_{li},\sigma_i\), profiles \(w^*,w^\star,W_l^*,W_l^\star\), rescalings \(w_{\lambda,\xi}^{*}(x)=w^{*}(\sqrt{\lambda}(x-\xi))\), \(W_{\lambda,\xi,l}^{*}(x)=W_l^{*}(\sqrt{\lambda}(x-\xi))\), \(w_{\lambda,\xi}^{\star}(x)=w^{\star}(\sqrt{\lambda}(x-\xi))\), \(W_{\lambda,\xi,l}^{\star}(x)=W_l^{\star}(\sqrt{\lambda}(x-\xi))\), and \(\rho_0^2=k\int_{\mathbb R^2}((w^*)^2+(w^\star)^2)\,dx\); what is the strongest existence statement that can be asserted for solutions of this form?

Let \(\Omega\subset \mathbb R^n\) be a bounded domain, \(T>0\), and \(\Omega_T:=\Omega\times(0,T)\). Write \(z=(x,t)\in\Omega_T\), let \(a:\Omega_T\to[0,\infty)\) be given, and define
\[
H(z,t):=t^p+a(z)t^q \qquad (t\ge 0).
\]
Assume \(\mathcal A:\Omega_T\times \mathbb R^{Nn}\to \mathbb R^{Nn}\) is a Carathéodory vector field such that for some constants \(0<\nu\le L<\infty\),
\[
\mathcal A(z,\xi)\cdot \xi\ge \nu\big(|\xi|^p+a(z)|\xi|^q\big),
\qquad
|\mathcal A(z,\xi)|\le L\big(|\xi|^{p-1}+a(z)|\xi|^{q-1}\big)
\]
for a.e. \(z\in\Omega_T\) and all \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{Nn}\). Let \(Q_\rho(z_0)\) denote a parabolic cylinder of radius \(\rho\) centered at \(z_0\). Suppose
\[
 u\in C(0,T;L^2(\Omega,\mathbb R^N))\cap L^q(0,T;W^{1,q}(\Omega,\mathbb R^N))\cap L^\infty(\Omega_T)
\]
is a weak solution in \(\Omega_T\) of
\[
 u_t-\operatorname{div}\mathcal A(z,\nabla u)=-\operatorname{div}\big(|F|^{p-2}F+a(z)|F|^{q-2}F\big).
\]
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the uniform higher integrability of \(\nabla u\)?

Let $\Gamma\subset M^3$ be a smooth closed immersed surface in a 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M^3$. Which of the following is the strongest statement about the quantity $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}(\Gamma)$ under these assumptions?

Let \((X^n,\omega)\) be a complete non-compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension \(n\), where \(\Ric_{\omega}\) denotes the Ricci \((1,1)\)-form of \(\omega\), and \(\Ric_{\omega}^n\) denotes its \(n\)-fold exterior product. Assume either that \((X^n,\omega)\) has positive sectional curvature, or more generally that \((X,\omega)\) has positive holomorphic bisectional curvature and admits a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion function (i.e. a smooth proper strictly plurisubharmonic function) whose gradient is uniformly bounded with respect to \(\omega\). What is the strongest universal estimate for the total integral \(\int_X \Ric_{\omega}^n\)?

Let $G$ be a finite primitive monolithic group (that is, a finite group with a unique minimal normal subgroup and a core-free maximal subgroup), and let $N=\operatorname{soc}(G)$ be its socle (the subgroup generated by the minimal normal subgroups of $G$). Recall that a group $H$ is a section of a group $K$ if $H$ is a quotient of a subgroup of $K$; a group is sectionally indecomposable if, whenever it is a section of $A\times B$, it is already a section of $A$ or of $B$. Which of the following statements is equivalent to saying that $G$ is sectionally indecomposable?

Let \(x:\Sigma\to \mathbb S^2\times \mathbb S^2\) be a minimal-Willmore surface (that is, a surface that is both minimal and Willmore, where a Willmore surface is a critical point of the Willmore functional). Which description gives the complete classification of such surfaces?

Let \(n\ge 2\) and let \(\theta\in M_n(\mathbb Q)\) be a rational skew-symmetric matrix. Let
\[
C^n_\theta=C(\mathbb S^{2n-1}_\theta):=C^*\!\left\langle \text{normal }T_1,\dots,T_n\ \middle|\ T_jT_i=e^{2\pi i\theta_{ij}}T_iT_j\ \forall i,j,\ \sum_i T_i^*T_i=1\right\rangle,
\]
the \(C^*\)-algebra of the odd quantum sphere \(\mathbb S^{2n-1}_\theta\). Let \(X\) be the compact Hausdorff space determined by \(C(X)=Z(C^n_\theta)\). For a \(C^*\)-bundle/sheaf \(\mathcal S\to X\), write \(\Gamma(\mathcal S)\) for its section algebra, \(\mathcal S_x\) for its fiber at \(x\in X\), and \(X_d:=\{x\in X: \dim \mathcal S_x=d\}\) for its dimensional strata. Which of the following is the strongest statement that can be proved about existence and structure in this setting?

Let a zonotope in $\mathbb{R}^d$ mean a Minkowski sum of finitely many line segments, and for $t>0$ write $tZ=\{tz:z\in Z\}$. Which of the following is the strongest correct statement of the form “there exists ... such that for all ...” about signed sums of points from a zonotope?

Let \(X\) be a Banach space such that its dual \(X^*\) has Rademacher type \(p\in(1,2]\) with type constant \(T_p(X^*)\), and fix an integer \(k\ge 1\). Define
\[
r_k(X)=6T_p(X^*)\,k^{-1+\frac1p}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal F\) be a finite family of convex sets in \(X\). Assume that for every choice of \(k\) sets \(K_1,\dots,K_k\in\mathcal F\), the intersection of those sets with the unit ball \(B_X=\{x\in X:\|x\|\le 1\}\) is nonempty:
\[
B_X\cap \bigcap_{i=1}^k K_i\neq\varnothing.
\]
Here \(\operatorname{dist}(x,K)=\inf\{\|x-y\|:y\in K\}\). Which of the following is the strongest consequence of these assumptions?

Let \(\mathcal F\) be the family consisting of all Mazur \(4\)-manifolds and all Jester \(4\)-manifolds, each regarded as a smooth, compact, contractible \(4\)-manifold, and write \(\partial M\) for the boundary of \(M\). Which statement is the strongest consequence that holds for every pair of distinct manifolds \(M,N\in\mathcal F\) about their boundaries?

Let \(N\ge 1\), \(m\ge 2\), and assume the following: \(1<p<\frac{2^*}{2}\) if \(N\ge 3\), and \(p>1\) if \(N=1,2\), where \(2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}\) for \(N\ge 3\); \(\mu_i>0\) for \(i=1,\dots,m\); \(\lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{ji}<0\) for all \(i\ne j\); and \(Q_\varepsilon(x-y_i):=Q(\varepsilon x-y_i)\), where \(Q\in C(\mathbb{R}^N)\) is nonnegative, has bounded support, and there exist exactly pairwise distinct points \(y_1,\dots,y_m\in\mathbb{R}^N\) such that \(Q(-y_i)=\|Q\|_\infty\) for all \(i=1,\dots,m\). For \(\varepsilon>0\), consider the coupled elliptic system
\[
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u_i + u_i
= \mu_i Q_\varepsilon(x-y_i) |u_i|^{2p-2}u_i
+ \displaystyle\sum_{j\neq i} \lambda_{ij} |u_j|^{p} |u_i|^{p-2}u_i, \\[4pt]
u_i \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N),\quad i=1,\dots,m,
\end{cases}
\]
and write \(\mathbf u=(u_1,\dots,u_m)\in H\) with \(H=(H^1(\mathbb R^N))^m\). Let \(J_\varepsilon\) denote the associated energy functional. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of sign-changing solutions for this system under these assumptions?

Let $m,r\in\mathbb N$, and let $[N]=\{1,2,\dots,N\}$. Suppose there is an $r$-coloring of $[N]$ (that is, an assignment of one of $r$ colors to each element of $[N]$) such that there is no monochromatic solution with all variables in $[N]$ to
\[
x_1+\cdots+x_{m+1}=y_1+\cdots+y_m,
\]
where “monochromatic” means that all numbers $x_1,\dots,x_{m+1},y_1,\dots,y_m$ receive the same color. Which of the following is the strongest consequence of these assumptions?

Let \(\hat{\mathbb R}=\mathbb R\times\{+,-\}\). Define
\[
\Phi=\Big\{\varphi:\hat{\mathbb R}\to \mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}:\ \varphi(\xi)>-\infty\text{ for only countably many }\xi\Big\},
\]
and for \(\varphi\in\Phi\) let
\[
\Lambda_\varphi=\{\xi\in\hat{\mathbb R}:\varphi(\xi)>-\infty\}.
\]
Also define
\[
(W\star\varphi)(x,t)=\sup_{\xi\in\hat{\mathbb R}}\big[W^{\xi}(0,0;x,t)+\varphi(\xi)\big],
\]
where \(W^{\xi}\) is the family of Busemann functions indexed by \(\xi\in\hat{\mathbb R}\). By the paper's convention, if \(\xi=(\eta,\sigma)\in\hat{\mathbb R}\), then expressions such as \(\xi^2\) mean \(\eta^2\). Almost surely, which statement is equivalent to saying that \(b\) is an eternal solution of the KPZ fixed point?

Let $A$ be a finite set and let $X \subset A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ be a subshift of finite type (for the usual shift action on $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$). Which of the following statements is equivalent to both "$X$ is surjunctive" and "$X$ is Moore"?

Let $(X,0)$ be a germ of a normal complex analytic surface. Write ${}^pIC_X\mathbb Z$ for the perverse intersection complex of $X$ with integral coefficients, and ${}^p_+IC_X\mathbb Z$ for the corresponding $p_+$-intermediate extension with integral coefficients. Set $E:=H^0({}^p_+IC_X\mathbb Z)_0$, i.e. the stalk at $0$ of the zeroth cohomology sheaf. What is the strongest statement that holds for every such germ about the natural morphism ${}^pIC_X\mathbb Z\to {}^p_+IC_X\mathbb Z$ (in the derived category) and the group $E$?

For a closed oriented smooth 4-manifold, let $b_2^+$ and $b_2^-$ denote the dimensions of maximal positive- and negative-definite subspaces of its intersection form, and call the manifold irreducible if every connected-sum decomposition has a summand homeomorphic to $S^4$. Let $D_\infty$ denote the infinite dihedral group (equivalently $\mathbb{Z}\rtimes \mathbb{Z}_2$ with nontrivial action). Fix integers $a,b\ge 12$. Which statement gives the strongest existence result for closed smooth 4-manifolds with fundamental group isomorphic to $D_\infty$ under these assumptions?

Let $G$ be a Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, and let $\alpha:G\to G$ be a continuous group endomorphism. Write $\operatorname d\alpha:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g$ for the differential of $\alpha$ at the identity. For a compatible metric $d$ on $G$, a sequence $(x_k)$ is called a $\delta$-pseudo-orbit of $\alpha$ if $d(\alpha(x_k),x_{k+1})<\delta$ whenever both terms are defined, and it is $\varepsilon$-shadowed by a point $x\in G$ if $d(\alpha^k(x),x_k)<\varepsilon$ for every defined index $k$. We say that $\alpha$ has the shadowing property if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that every infinite $\delta$-pseudo-orbit is $\varepsilon$-shadowed. Also, $\operatorname d\alpha$ is called hyperbolic if its complexification has no eigenvalue of modulus $1$. Which statement holds for every such pair $(G,\alpha)$?

Fix a depth parameter \(\delta>0\), and let \(T^\delta\) be the singular integral operator
\[
(T^\delta f)(x)=\frac{1}{2\delta}\,\mathrm{P.V.}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\coth\!\left(\frac{\pi (y-x)}{2\delta}\right)f(y)\,dy.
\]
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge 1\), let \(\mathbf c=(c_1,\dots,c_n)\) satisfy \(0<c_1<\cdots<c_n\), let \(\mathbf x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(U^{(n)}(\cdot,\cdot;\mathbf c,\mathbf x)\) be the corresponding \(n\)-soliton solution of
\[
u_t+\frac{1}{\delta}u_x+2uu_x+T^\delta u_{xx}=0
\quad\text{on }\mathbb R\times\mathbb R.
\]
What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the uniform orbital stability in \(H^{n/2}(\mathbb R)\) of perturbations of \(U^{(n)}(0,\cdot;\mathbf c,\mathbf x)\)?

Fix \(m>0\). For an admissible rank-two orthogonal projection
\[
\gamma=|u_1\rangle\langle u_1|+|u_2\rangle\langle u_2|,
\]
with \(u_1,u_2\in H^{1/2}(\mathbb R^3,\mathbb C)\) and \(\langle u_i,u_j\rangle_{L^2}=\delta_{ij}\), define
\[
\mathcal E_a(\gamma):=\operatorname{tr}(\sqrt{-\Delta+m^2}-m)\gamma-a\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho_\gamma(x)^{4/3}\,dx,
\qquad \rho_\gamma(x)=|u_1(x)|^2+|u_2(x)|^2.
\]
Let
\[
E_a(2)=\inf\Big\{\mathcal E_a(\gamma):\ \gamma=|u_1\rangle\langle u_1|+|u_2\rangle\langle u_2|,\ u_1,u_2\in H^{1/2}(\mathbb R^3,\mathbb C),\ \langle u_i,u_j\rangle_{L^2}=\delta_{ij}\Big\},\qquad a>0.
\]
Let \(D_{4/3,2}>0\) denote the constant appearing in the corresponding Lieb--Thirring-type inequality for such rank-two projections (that is, the quantity called \(D_{p,N}\) at \(p=4/3\) and \(N=2\)). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about existence of minimizers of \(E_a(2)\) as \(a\) varies?

Let $G$ be a normally poly-surface group of length $n$, meaning that $G$ admits a normal series
$$1=G_0\triangleleft G_1\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft G_n=G$$
whose successive quotients $G_i/G_{i-1}$ are surface groups. Let $\mathcal{VC}$ denote the family of virtually cyclic subgroups of $G$, and denote by $\gdvc(G)$ the geometric dimension of $G$ for this family, i.e. the minimal dimension of a model for $E_{\mathcal{VC}}G$. Which of the following is the strongest statement that holds for every such group $G$?

Let \(\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) be a connected mean convex region (that is, each boundary component has nonnegative mean curvature with respect to the inward unit normal), and suppose that \(\partial\Omega\) has at least two connected components. For a boundary component \(\Sigma\subset \partial\Omega\), let \(H_\Sigma\) denote the mean curvature of \(\Sigma\) computed with respect to the inward unit normal. Which statement is the strongest one that holds for every boundary component \(\Sigma\) of \(\partial\Omega\)?

Let \(\mathrm{Homeo}_0(S)\) denote the group of homeomorphisms of a surface \(S\) that are isotopic to the identity. For \(G=\mathrm{Homeo}_0(S)\), let \([G,G]\) denote its commutator subgroup, and for \(g\in [G,G]\), let \(\operatorname{cl}_G(g)\) be the commutator length of \(g\), i.e. the least number of commutators in \(G\) whose product is \(g\). For \(S\in\{\mathbb{R}\mathrm{P}^2, M\}\), where \(M\) is the Möbius strip, what is the strongest statement that can be proved about commutator length on \([\mathrm{Homeo}_0(S),\mathrm{Homeo}_0(S)]\)?

Consider the following finite collection of objects, each viewed in its corresponding Mukai model (that is, the relevant geometric invariant theory (GIT) quotient: for curve cases, Mukai's model of the appropriate moduli space of curves; for surface cases, Mukai's model of the appropriate moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces). 

Genus 7: the genus 7 tangent developable; the genus 7 cuspidal cubic with 7-gonal symmetry; the genus 7 balanced K3 carpet; the genus 7 balanced ribbon; and the genus 7 graph curve associated to the fixed graph \(\Gamma_7\). 

Genus 8: the genus 8 tangent developable; the genus 8 cuspidal cubic with 8-gonal symmetry; a genus 8 reducible surface with four components, each generically nonreduced; a genus 8 reducible curve with five components, each generically nonreduced; and the genus 8 graph curve associated to the fixed graph \(\Gamma_8\). 

Genus 9: the genus 9 tangent developable; the genus 9 cuspidal cubic with 9-gonal symmetry; the genus 9 balanced K3 carpet; the genus 9 balanced ribbon; and the genus 9 graph curve associated to the fixed graph \(\Gamma_9\). 

Genus 10: the genus 10 tangent developable; the genus 10 cuspidal cubic with 10-gonal symmetry; a genus 10 reducible surface with two components, each generically nonreduced; and a genus 10 reducible curve with four components, each generically nonreduced. 

Which of the following is the strongest statement that holds for every object in this collection?

For integers \(k_1,k_2\ge 2\), let \(n(k_1,k_2)\) denote the minimum number of vertices in a graph in which every vertex is contained in both a clique of size \(k_1\) and an independent set of size \(k_2\). What is the strongest universal lower bound on \(n(k_1,k_2)\), including the stated equality case?

Let $L$ be a hyperbolic link in $S^3$ with $\ell$ components $L_1,\ldots,L_\ell$, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\ell\in[0,\pi]$. Let $M_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\ell}(L)$ denote the hyperbolic cone manifold with singular set $L$ whose cone angle around $L_i$ is $\alpha_i$ (assuming this cone manifold is hyperbolic). For an odd integer $r\ge 3$, let $V_{j_1,\ldots,j_\ell}^{(r)}(L)$ be the colored Jones invariant of $L$ in which $L_i$ is colored by a weight $j_i\in\{j/2\mid j\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le j\le r-2\}$, evaluated at $q=\exp(4\pi\sqrt{-1}/r)$, and write $r=2n+1$. For each $i=1,\ldots,\ell$, let $j_i=j_i(n)$ be weights such that
\[
\left|8\pi\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{j_i}{2n+1}-2\pi\right|=\alpha_i.
\]
Write $\mathrm{Vol}(M_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\ell}(L))$ for the hyperbolic volume of $M_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_\ell}(L)$. Which of the following is the strongest explicit asymptotic conclusion for the quantities $V_{j_1,\ldots,j_\ell}^{(2n+1)}(L)$ under these assumptions?

What is the strongest statement that holds for every pair \((X,w)\) with the following properties: \(X=(\mathcal N,\mathcal W,\mathbf r)\) is a fully connected algebraic network, where \(\mathcal N_t\) denotes the vector space at layer \(t\) and \(r_t\) the activation degree at layer \(t\); the layer widths \(\dim \mathcal N_t\) are non-increasing and the output layer is scalar (i.e. \(\dim \mathcal N_{\mathrm{out}}=1\)); for each layer \(t\) either \(r_t\ge 3\), or \(r_t=2\) and \(\dim \mathcal N_t=\dim \mathcal N_{t+1}\); \(w\in\mathcal W\) is a parameter point of \(X\) (so \(w\) is a tuple of layer matrices); and \(\Phi_X(w)\) is singular, where \(\Phi_X\) is the realization map associated to \(X\)?

Let \(q\) be an indeterminate, write \([m]=(1-q^m)/(1-q)\), let \((a;r)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-ar^j)\) for \(k\ge 0\), and let \(\Phi_n(q)\) denote the \(n\)th cyclotomic polynomial. For an integer \(n>1\) with \(n\equiv 1\pmod 4\), define
\[
S_n(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{(n-1)/2} [4k+1]\,\frac{(q;q^2)_k^3}{(q^2;q^2)_k^3}\,q^{k(n^2-2nk-n-2)/4}.
\]
Which congruence modulo a polynomial holds for \(S_n(q)\) (interpreting congruences of rational functions in the reduced-denominator sense)?

Fix a depth \(L \ge 1\), input dimension \(d_{\mathrm{in}}\), output dimension \(d_{\mathrm{out}} \ge 1\), and Lipschitz activation functions \(\sigma^{(1)}, \ldots, \sigma^{(L)}\). For each \(n\), let \(f_{(n)}^{(L)} : \mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{in}}} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}}\) be the output of a fully connected feedforward neural network with hidden-layer widths \(n_\ell = n_\ell(n)\), where \(n_0 := d_{\mathrm{in}}\), satisfying \(\lim_{n\to\infty} n_\ell / n \in (0,\infty]\) for every \(\ell = 1, \ldots, L-1\), and with i.i.d. Gaussian weights \(W_{i,j}^{(\ell)}\) such that \(\mathbb{E}[(W_{i,j}^{(\ell)})^2] = 1 / n_{\ell-1}\) for every layer \(\ell\) and every \(i,j\) (LeCun initialization). For a compact input set \(X \subset \mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{in}}}\), consider the rescaled random function \(x \mapsto (1/\sqrt{n}) f_{(n)}^{(L)}(x)\) as an element of \(C(X, \mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}})\) equipped with the topology of uniform convergence. If, for each finite subset \(X_0 \subset X\), \(\pi_{X_0}(z)\) denotes the restriction of \(z \in C(X, \mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}})\) to \(X_0\), and \(I_{X_0,\mathrm{out}}^{(L)}\) is the finite-dimensional rate function for the projected process on \((\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}})^{X_0}\), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the asymptotic behavior, as \(n \to \infty\), of the laws of \(x \mapsto (1/\sqrt{n}) f_{(n)}^{(L)}(x)\) on \(C(X,\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{out}}})\)?

Let $(M^n,g,k)$, with $n\ge 3$, be a complete asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set on an $n$-dimensional manifold $M^n$, where $g$ is the Riemannian metric, $k$ is the second fundamental form, and $(E,P)$ denotes its total energy--momentum vector. Assume the dominant energy condition holds, namely
\[
\mu\ge |J|_g,
\]
where $\mu$ and $J$ are the energy and momentum densities. Which of the following is the strongest consequence of these assumptions?

Fix $n\ge 1$, $\alpha>0$, and $s\ge 0$. For a finite Borel measure $\eta$ on $\mathbb R^m$, write $I_\alpha(\eta)=\iint |u-v|^{-\alpha}\,d\eta(u)\,d\eta(v)$, and let $e^{it\Delta}$ be the Schr\"odinger propagator on $\mathbb R^n$. Here $B_m(0,1)$ denotes the unit ball in $\mathbb R^m$, and when $\nu$ is supported in $B_{n+1}(0,1)$ we view $\mathbb R^{n+1}=\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$ with coordinates $(x,t)$. Assume there is a constant $C_{\alpha,s}$ such that for every finite Borel measure $\mu$ supported in $B_n(0,1)$ and every Schwartz function $g\in \mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$,
\[ \int \sup_{0<t<1}\big|e^{it\Delta}g(x)\big|\,d\mu(x)\le C_{\alpha,s}\, I_\alpha(\mu)^{1/2}\,\|g\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^n)}. \]
What is the strongest uniform consequence of this assumption of the form "there exists a constant such that for all measures and all test functions ..."?

Let $d\in\{1,2\}$, $\gamma>0$, and $\lambda,\omega\in\mathbb R$. Let $A$ be the self-adjoint operator associated with the Anderson Hamiltonian with spatial white noise $\xi$ in dimension $d$, let $\mu_0$ denote the lowest eigenvalue of $-A$, and let $\mathrm D(\sqrt{|A|})$ be the domain of $\sqrt{|A|}$. Consider the equation
\[
-A\phi-\lambda|\phi|^{2\gamma}\phi+\omega\phi=0
\]
for $\phi\in \mathrm D(\sqrt{|A|})$. Here, a positive solution means a solution with $\phi>0$, and a non-trivial non-negative solution means $\phi\ge 0$ and $\phi\not\equiv 0$. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the exact criterion for existence of positive solutions, together with the corresponding nonexistence of non-trivial non-negative solutions for the remaining parameter regimes?

Let \(\mathfrak{s}\) be a seaweed subalgebra of a complex simple Lie algebra, i.e. an intersection of two opposite parabolic subalgebras. Say that \(\mathfrak{s}\) is decomposable if it is a direct sum of two nonzero ideals, and indecomposable otherwise. Write \(\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{s})\) for the center of \(\mathfrak{s}\), write \(H^n(\mathfrak{s},\mathfrak{s})\) for the \(n\)-th Lie algebra cohomology of \(\mathfrak{s}\) with coefficients in the adjoint \(\mathfrak{s}\)-module, and write \(\bigwedge^i \mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{s})^\ast\) for the \(i\)-th exterior power of the dual of the center. Which of the following is the strongest conclusion that holds, distinguishing the indecomposable and decomposable cases for \(\mathfrak{s}\)?

Let A be a (not necessarily unital) JB*-algebra, with norm ‖·‖ and Jordan product ∘. Assume that A is associative with respect to ∘, and that A contains no 2-nilpotent elements, meaning there is no nonzero x in A such that x ∘ x = 0. Which statement is equivalent to both of these properties?

Let \(u\) be the solution to the one-dimensional stochastic wave equation
\[
\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}(t,x)+u(t,x)\,\dot X(t,x),\qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R,
\]
with initial conditions \(u(0,x)=1\) and \(\partial_t u(0,x)=0\), where \(X\) is the Lévy colored noise from the setup. Suppose Assumption B holds, and let \(x\mapsto u(t,x)\) denote the spatial random field at a fixed time \(t>0\). What is the strongest statement that can be proved about the field \(\{u(t,x)\}_{x\in\mathbb R}\) for every \(t>0\)?

Assume that the standing hypotheses called Conditions 1 and 2 hold. Let $v>0$, let $W$ be a $d$-dimensional Brownian motion, and let $(\bar{\mathfrak P}(t,p,q),\bar{\mathfrak Q}(t,p,q))$ denote the solution of the underdamped Langevin equation
\[
\mathrm d\bar{\mathfrak P}(t)=-\nabla V(\bar{\mathfrak Q}(t))\,\mathrm dt-v\bar{\mathfrak P}(t)\,\mathrm dt+\mathrm dW(t),\qquad
\mathrm d\bar{\mathfrak Q}(t)=\bar{\mathfrak P}(t)\,\mathrm dt,
\]
with initial data $(\bar{\mathfrak P}(0),\bar{\mathfrak Q}(0))=(p,q)$. Let $\zeta_\alpha:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ satisfy
\[
|\zeta_\alpha(q)|\le L_1(\|q\|^{\beta_1}+1)\qquad\text{for all }q\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
with $\beta_1\in(0,1)$ and $L_1>0$. Let $V\in C^\infty_{\rm p}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R)$ (smooth with polynomial growth) satisfy $V(q)\ge 0$ for all $q\in\mathbb R^d$, and assume there exist $\alpha_0>0$ and $\alpha_1\in(0,1)$ such that
\[
\frac12\langle \nabla V(q),q\rangle\ge \alpha_1V(q)+v^2\frac{\alpha_1(2-\alpha_1)}{8(1-\alpha_1)}\|q\|^2-\alpha_0
\qquad\text{for all }q\in\mathbb R^d.
\]
Fix $\alpha>\frac{v^2}{4}$ and $C_V\ge 0$, and define
\[
U_\alpha(q):=V(q)-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|q\|^2+C_V.
\]
Fix $(p,q)\in\mathbb R^{2d}$, let $t_n=n\tau$, and define $\Delta W_n=W(t_{n+1})-W(t_n)$. Consider the DSAV scheme
\[
\bar{\mathfrak P}_n:=P_n-\frac v2 Q_n,\qquad \bar{\mathfrak Q}_n:=Q_n,
\]
with initial data
\[
(P_0,Q_0,r_0)=\left(p+\frac v2 q,\,q,\,\sqrt{U_\alpha(q)}\right),
\]
and updates
\[
\frac{P_{n+1}-P_n}{\tau}=\frac{r_{n+1}}{\sqrt{U_\alpha(Q_n)}}\bigl(-\nabla V(Q_n)+\alpha Q_n\bigr)-\frac v2 P_{n+1}+\left(\frac{v^2}{4}-\alpha\right)Q_{n+1}+\tau^{-1}\Delta W_n,
\]
\[
\frac{Q_{n+1}-Q_n}{\tau}=P_{n+1}-\frac v2 Q_{n+1},
\]
\[
\frac{r_{n+1}-r_n}{\tau}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{U_\alpha(Q_n)}}\langle \nabla V(Q_n)-\alpha Q_n, P_{n+1}\rangle-\frac v4\beta_0 r_{n+1}-v\zeta_\alpha(Q_n),
\]
where $\beta_0$ is the fixed constant appearing in the DSAV method. What is the strongest uniform weak-error estimate that holds for every test function $\varphi\in C^\infty_{\rm p}(\mathbb R^{2d};\mathbb R)$?

Let \(k\ge 1\) be an integer, and let \(G\) be a finite simple graph on \(n\) vertices. The edge-connectivity of a graph is the minimum size of an edge-cut. Call \(G\) \(k\)-edge-maximal if every subgraph of \(G\) has edge-connectivity at most \(k\), but for every missing edge \(e\), the graph \(G+e\) obtained by adding \(e\) contains a subgraph with edge-connectivity at least \(k+1\). Which statement is the strongest consequence that holds for every such graph?

Let \(k\ge 2\) be an integer, and for a graph \(G\), let \(\lambda_k(G)\) denote the \(k\)-th largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of \(G\). For a graph \(G\) on \(n\) vertices, which of the following is the strongest universal upper bound on \(\lambda_k(G)\)?

Let \(f\) be a rational map of degree \(d\ge 2\). Assume that \(f\) has two invariant Fatou components \(U\) and \(V\) (here a Fatou component means a connected component of the Fatou set \(F(f)\)), that \(U\) is completely invariant (that is, \(f(U)=U\) and \(f^{-1}(U)=U\)) while \(V\) is invariant but not completely invariant, and that every critical value of \(f\) lies in \(U\cup V\). Which of the following is the strongest conclusion about the Julia set \(J(f)\)?

Let $\Omega$ be a nondegenerate skew-symmetric form on $\mathbb{C}^4$, and let
$$F=\{(V_1,V_2)\in \mathrm{G}(1,4)\times \mathrm{G}(2,4)\mid V_1\subset V_2,\ \text{and }V_1,V_2\text{ are }\Omega\text{-isotropic}\}$$
be the complete flag variety of $\Omega$-isotropic lines contained in $\Omega$-isotropic planes in $\mathbb{C}^4$. Let $H\subset \mathrm{PSP}(4)$, where $\mathrm{PSP}(4)$ is the projective symplectic group of $\Omega$, be the complex torus of homothety classes of diagonal matrices acting naturally on $F$. What is the normalized Chow quotient $X$ of $F$ by $H$?

Let \(\mathscr{A}=\{H_1,\ldots,H_n\}\) be a generic central arrangement of hyperplanes in \(\mathbb{R}^3\) (that is, each \(H_i\) passes through the origin and no three hyperplanes intersect along a line), let \(\br\colon \mathscr{A}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge -1}\) be a smoothness distribution, and let \(\Sigma^{\mathscr{A}}\) be the fan of \(\mathscr{A}\). For each \(i\), choose a linear form \(\ell_i\in R=\mathbb{R}[x,y,z]\) vanishing on \(H_i\), and write \(\bm{\ell}^{\br}=(\ell_1^{\br(H_1)+1},\ldots,\ell_n^{\br(H_n)+1})\). For each degree \(d\ge 0\), let \(\mathcal{S}^{\br}_d(\Sigma^{\mathscr{A}})\) denote the space of splines on \(\Sigma^{\mathscr{A}}\) whose restriction to each region is a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(d\), with smoothness \(\br(H_i)\) across \(H_i\). If \(\HK_i(\bm{\ell}^{\br})\) denotes the \(i\)-th Koszul homology module of the sequence \(\bm{\ell}^{\br}\), which statement gives the strongest uniform conclusion valid for every such arrangement, smoothness distribution, and degree?

Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $G$ be a finite $p$-group, and let $C$ be a $\mathbb{Z}_p[G]$-lattice, meaning a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}_p[G]$-module that is free as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module. Assume that $$(C\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p} \mathbb{Q}_p)\oplus \mathbb{Q}_p$$ is a free $\mathbb{Q}_p[G]$-module. Here an unramified $G$-extension $K/k$ means an unramified Galois extension of number fields with Galois group $G$; if $E_K$ denotes the unit group of $K$, then $\mathcal{E}_{K,p}=E_K\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Z}_p$. Which of the following is the strongest existence statement that holds under these assumptions?

Let \(0<r<R\), let \(A=A(r,R)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: r<|z|<R\}\), and define the Cauchy transform on the annulus by
\[
(C_A f)(z)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_A \frac{f(w)}{z-w}\,dA(w),\qquad z\in A,\ f\in L^2(A),
\]
where \(dA\) denotes planar area measure. If \(J_\nu\) and \(Y_\nu\) denote the Bessel functions of the first and second kind, respectively, which statement about the \(L^2(A)\to L^2(A)\) operator norm of \(C_A\) holds?

Let $A=(V_m,S_n,\pi,\lambda)$ be a full Mealy automaton, where $V_m$ and $S_n$ are finite alphabets of sizes $m$ and $n$, respectively, meaning a finite letter-to-letter transducer with all transitions defined, and let
\[
\theta_A:S_n\times V_m\to V_m\times S_n,\qquad \theta_A(s,v)=(\lambda(s,v),\pi(s,v))
\]
be its associated bijection. Let $F=F_{\theta_A}$ be the associated one-vertex rank-two graph, and let $Y=Y_A$ be the associated $VH$-square complex (the square complex with one vertex, vertical edges indexed by $V_m$, horizontal edges indexed by $S_n$, and one square for each pair in $V_m\times S_n$). Here, "$A$ is bi-reversible" means that the automaton is reversible/invertible in both the automaton and dual senses, "$F$ is aperiodic" means aperiodic as a rank-two graph, and "$Y$ contains an anti-torus" means that $Y$ has a horizontal-vertical flat whose corresponding horizontal and vertical directions have no nontrivial commuting powers. Which of the following is the strongest consequence of these assumptions?

Let \((M^n,h)\) be a connected compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension \(n\ge 2\) that is locally conformally K\"ahler (LCK), meaning its fundamental form \(\omega_h\) satisfies \(d\omega_h=\theta\wedge\omega_h\) for some closed real 1-form \(\theta\). Assume its Chern holomorphic sectional curvature (for the Chern connection of \(h\)) is constant, i.e. \(H_h^C\equiv c\) for some real constant \(c\). Which of the following is the strongest statement that holds for every such \((M^n,h)\)?

For each integer $n \ge 10$, let $X_n=2\mathbb{CP}^2\# n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$, where $\#$ denotes connected sum and $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ is $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with the opposite orientation. Let $T(X_n)$ denote the Torelli group of $X_n$, i.e. the subgroup of the mapping class group (smooth isotopy classes of diffeomorphisms of $X_n$) consisting of classes represented by diffeomorphisms continuously isotopic to the identity. What is the strongest statement that can be proved about homomorphisms from $T(X_n)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$?

Let \(X(1,3,9)=\mu_{13}\text{-}\operatorname{Hilb}(\mathbb C^3)\), where \(\mu_{13}\subset \mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)\) acts with weights \((1,3,9)\), and let \(D(X(1,3,9))\) denote the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on \(X(1,3,9)\). Let \((Q_1,W_1)\) be the quiver with potential associated with \(X(1,3,9)\), where the underlying quiver has vertices \(1,2,3,4,5,6\) and arrows \(a_1:1\to 2\), \(b_1:2\to 6\), \(c_1:6\to 1\), \(c_2:2\to 3\), \(a_2:3\to 4\), \(b_2:4\to 2\), \(b_3:6\to 4\), \(c_3:4\to 5\), and \(a_3:5\to 6\). Let \(\AT(Q_1,W_1)\) denote the associated algebraic braid twist group, and let \(T_k\) be the corresponding twist autoequivalences. A faithful action means an injective homomorphism into \(\operatorname{Aut}(D(X(1,3,9)))\). Which statement is the strongest existence claim about an action of \(\AT(Q_1,W_1)\) on \(D(X(1,3,9))\)?

Fix an integer \(N\ge 3\). In the normalized setting \(\|x_0-x_\star\|^2\le 1\), write the constant step as \(\alpha=1+\rho\), and let \(\rho_N\) denote the balanced root, i.e. the positive solution of
\[
\rho^{2N}(2N\rho+2N+1)=1.
\]
Suppose Systems C, A, and B are the coefficient-generating systems in this normalization: from parameters \(d_0,\ldots,d_{N-2}\) they produce coefficients \(c_0,\ldots,c_N\), \(a_0,\ldots,a_{N-1}\), and \(b_0,\ldots,b_{N-2}\), together with residual quantities \(\varepsilon_0,\ldots,\varepsilon_N\). A low-rank performance-estimation-problem (PEP) certificate is encoded by the multiplier pattern
\[
\lambda_{\star j}=c_j,\qquad
\lambda_{i,i+1}=a_i,\qquad
\lambda_{i+1,i}=b_i,\qquad
\lambda_{ij}=d_i c_j\quad(i+2\le j).
\]
What is the strongest existence statement that can be asserted in this setting?

For a prime $p$ and $m\ge 1$, let $\mathbb{Q}_p^{\times}$ denote the nonzero $p$-adic numbers, and consider the operator $D$ on $\mathbb{Q}_p^{\times}/p^{m\mathbb{Z}}$. Also let
\[
\boldsymbol{R}=(1-p^{-1})(\boldsymbol{P}-\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{P}\mathbf{1}_m)),\qquad (\boldsymbol{P})_{ij}=p^{-|i-j|},
\]
where $\mathbf{1}_m$ is the length-$m$ all-ones vector and $\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol v)$ denotes the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries given by the vector $\boldsymbol v$. Which description gives the complete spectrum of $D$ together with its multiplicities?

Let $0<\sigma_1<2$, $0<\sigma_2\le \sigma_1$, and $0<\sigma_3<\sigma_1$. Let $a\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ with $a\ge 0$, and let $V\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^3)$. Write $V_-(x)=\max\{-V(x),0\}$, $s_+=\max\{s,0\}$, and $\langle x\rangle=(1+|x|^2)^{1/2}$. Here $A\lesssim B$ means $A\le C B$ for some constant $C>0$ independent of $x$. Assume:

1. there exists $c_0>0$ such that
$$
V_-(x)+\big(\nabla V(x)\cdot x\big)_+\le c_0\,a(x)^{\frac{\sigma_3+1}{\sigma_2+1}} \quad \text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^3;
$$
2. the damping satisfies
$$
|\Delta a(x)|\lesssim
\begin{cases}
\langle x\rangle^{-7(\sigma_2+1)} & \text{if }0\le \sigma_2<\sigma_1,\\
\langle x\rangle^{-1} & \text{if }\sigma_2=\sigma_1;
\end{cases}
$$
3. if $\sigma_2\ne \sigma_3$, then
$$
V_-(x)+\big(\nabla V(x)\cdot x\big)_+\lesssim
\begin{cases}
\langle x\rangle^{-7(\sigma_3+1)} & \text{if }\sigma_3<\sigma_2,\\
\langle x\rangle^{-\frac{\sigma_3+1}{\sigma_1+1}} & \text{if }\sigma_3>\sigma_2.
\end{cases}
$$

For $u_0\in H^1(\mathbb R^3)$, consider the Cauchy problem
$$
\begin{cases}
 i\partial_t u+\Delta u+i\,a(x)|u|^{2\sigma_2}u=|u|^{2\sigma_1}u+V(x)|u|^{2\sigma_3}u,\\
 u(0,x)=u_0(x).
\end{cases}
$$
What is the strongest statement that can be asserted about existence in this setting?

Let \(G\) be a second-countable locally compact abelian group. Suppose \(f\in C_u(G)\) is mean almost periodic with respect to a Følner sequence \(\mathcal A\), or \(\mu\in \mathcal M^\infty(G)\) is a translation-bounded measure that is mean almost periodic with respect to a van Hove sequence \(\mathcal A\).
